item.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
item.description: Paradromics has announced a strategic partnership with Nvidia to utilize the latter's AI hardware and software stack to miniaturize brain signal decoding systems. The collaboration focuses on replacing current bulky, cart-based electronics with portable terminal devices, leveraging edge computing to process massive neural datasets in real-time.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra model successfully generated a machine-verifiable proof for the Smoktunowicz gap theorem on the Autoform-Hard benchmark, overcoming missing mathematical foundations in the library. By autonomously selecting a new research-based proof strategy, the model produced 1,800 lines of Lean code, signaling a transition from heuristic searching to creative proof generation in AI reasoning.

item.title: Marlowe Raises $277 Million to Bolster Alternatives to Nvidia Chips
item.description: AI infrastructure startup Marlowe has secured $277 million in funding to develop compute infrastructure utilizing AMD accelerators as an alternative to Nvidia hardware. The company plans to deploy its first data center by the end of 2026, aiming to challenge Nvidia's market dominance.

item.title: Bret Taylor’s Sierra Finalizing More Than $1.75 Billion Round
item.description: Customer service AI startup Sierra, founded by Bret Taylor, is finalizing a funding round exceeding $1.75 billion, led by Lightspeed and Greenoaks. The transaction values the company at $30 billion, up from $15.8 billion in May, reflecting intense investor confidence in AI-driven enterprise service automation.

Will it bring on total societal collapse? Though there’s room for disagreement about which catastrophe is most salient, experts are aligned on the idea that society is, for one reason or another, in real trouble. item.title: How Nvidia fought for years in Washington to sell its prized chips to China
item.description: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's political influence has collapsed following revelations of his involvement with a woman suspected of espionage for China, whose firm is under investigation for illicit trade of Nvidia chips. Previously, Nvidia employed aggressive lobbying to circumvent export restrictions and resisted mandatory chip-tracking regulations by claiming compliance was technically impossible, causing severe backlash and deep distrust among U.S. lawmakers.

item.title: US ports face cyber attack onslaught as hackers target vital trade routes
item.description: Kent Britton, CEO of the Port of Corpus Christi, reported that the port faces thousands of daily network intrusion attempts. The FBI has warned that malicious actors are increasingly deploying an AI tool dubbed 'Artex' to automate the exploitation of software vulnerabilities within ports and shipping infrastructure, shifting from password spraying to sophisticated executive phishing.

item.title: Meta Muse can now do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
item.description: Walmart has integrated Meta’s Muse AI agent through its recently announced Agent Gateway. Customers can authorize Muse via 'Agent Profiles' to autonomously browse and purchase products, with built-in spending limits, manual approval requirements, and privacy protections to prevent purchase history leakage.

item.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
item.description: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing Elon Musk’s SpaceX, alleging that the company violated consumer protection laws by lying to users about both the safety of its generative AI tools and how seriously the company took stopping child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and nonconsensual intimate imagery (NCII) from proliferating on its platforms. item.title: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
item.description: Research by CarbonPlan suggests that 'Enhanced Rock Weathering' (ERW), a climate solution heavily backed by Google and Microsoft, faces significant scalability challenges. The study indicates that spreading basalt or olivine at levels required for climate impact may degrade soil health and decrease crop yields; scaling back applications to protect harvests would likely cap the method's CO2 removal potential to under 1 billion tons per year.

item.title: Crowdstrike Reaches 44 Billion Cybersecurity Deal For Zscaler
item.description: CrowdStrike has entered an all-stock acquisition agreement to purchase Zscaler in a deal valued at approximately $43.9 billion. The merger combines CrowdStrike’s endpoint security with Zscaler’s zero-trust network offerings to meet enterprise demand for vendor consolidation, with Zscaler shareholders receiving 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, resulting in existing CrowdStrike shareholders owning 84.1% of the new entity.

item.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a 750B-parameter flagship model built on its Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T models (Z.ai)
item.description: Z.ai has launched its flagship model, GLM-5.4, utilizing the proprietary 'Loop Transformer' architecture. By scaling loop depth alongside total parameter size, the 750B-parameter model achieves performance benchmarks comparable to 2T-3T scale models, signaling a significant breakthrough in architectural efficiency.

item.title: Ex-Sequoia Boss Backs UK Defense Startup at $450 Million Value
item.description: European defense AI startup Agon has raised $70 million in a Series A round, valuing the firm at $450 million to develop foundational infrastructure for agentic warfare. The round, led by Northzone, marks the first joint investment from the UK Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund, with participation from former Sequoia global leader Roelof Botha.

item.title: Trump hosts crypto traders as demand for his meme coin fades
item.description: Former U.S. President Donald Trump hosted a crypto investor reception at his Northern Virginia golf club, aiming to re-engage high-net-worth holders and revive the market interest in his meme coins. Trump explicitly called for Congress to enact a federal regulatory framework for digital assets, attempting to align his political agenda with the industry's push for legal clarity.

item.title: Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate
item.description: Researchers at the Academy of Military Science in Beijing warn that the U.S. integration of AI into nuclear decision-making could compress response times from 15-30 minutes to under 90 seconds. This capability sparks concerns that U.S. forces may achieve superior precision in detecting and neutralizing Chinese nuclear assets, thereby undermining Beijing's second-strike deterrence.

item.title: Governors Call for Federal AI Rules Without Sidelining States
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom released a framework for AI governance, proposing baseline safety standards, mandatory third-party audits, emergency shutdown authorities, and limits on recursive self-improvement. The initiative aims to fill federal regulatory voids by imposing legal oversight on AI models with extreme catastrophic risk potential.

item.title: Amazon’s AI resistance: workers ready for battle over data centres
item.description: Tech company's plans for rapid expansion face opposition from the public and its own employees

item.title: Boston-based Aevius, whose foundation models analyze patient health using medical records, imaging, and other data, raised a $22M seed led by Insight Partners (Katherine Davis/Axios)
item.description: Clinical intelligence startup Aevius has raised $22 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners. The founding team, leveraging their successful track record in selling clinical AI assets to Big Pharma, will focus on building foundation models that analyze EHRs, medical imaging, and multi-modal health data.

item.title: Ant Group Bets on Simplexity to Thrive in China's Humanoid Race
item.description: Simplexity Robotics announced that it has received $100 million led by new investor Ant Group Co., Ltd. on November 23, 2026. The company issued convertible preferred shares in the transaction. The transaction includes participation from returning investors Alibaba Group Holding Limited, HongShan Capital Advisors Limited, Tencent Holdings Limited and BlueRun Investment Consulting (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. The company raised funding at a post-money valuation of $1,600 million. This super rating is th

item.title: Compute Desk, which is building capital markets infrastructure to price, trade, hedge, and clear compute, raised a $45M seed round led by Lightspeed (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
item.description: Compute Desk raised $45 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Led by CEO Andrawes Bahou, the startup aims to build capital markets infrastructure to turn compute into a tradable, hedgeable asset, addressing the growing financialization of AI hardware resources.

item.title: Trump’s AI Chip Crackdown Inflicts Collateral Damage Across Asia
item.description: China has warned that it will take action to defend its interests after US President Donald Trump's administration introduced tougher restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, escalating tensions over technology access just as the two countries prepare for high-level talks.The measures could also disrupt Southeast Asia's rapidly expanding technology industry, where billions of dollars are being invested in data centres powered by American-made processors.On Monday, 16 November

item.title: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
item.description: London-based legal tech firm Alecto raised $20 million in a seed round led by Insight Partners. Founded by Will Rice, the firm aims to leverage AI to automate complex property conveyancing tasks in the UK, challenging traditional hourly billing models to improve transparency and consumer outcomes by 2027.

item.title: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating (Kim Woo-young/CHOSUNBIZ)
item.description: Private equity firm MBK Partners has signed a tender offer agreement to take Japanese digital pen technology firm Wacom private in a deal valued at approximately 1.16 trillion yen. Samsung Electronics, a key strategic partner, will participate by tendering its current stake and reinvesting in the acquiring entity, retaining a roughly 6.3% stake to ensure ongoing technological collaboration.

item.title: Arva AI, which builds AI agents for banks' financial-crime compliance teams and counts Wise as a customer, raised a $20M Series A led by Arthur Ventures (Ryan Lawler/Axios)
item.description: Arva AI has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Arthur Ventures to advance its AI agent-based compliance automation for the banking sector. The company focuses on streamlining financial crime compliance reviews to minimize human error and operational latency.

item.title: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay
item.description: BILL Holdings has reached a definitive agreement to be taken private in an all-cash transaction led by TPG, with a total valuation of approximately $6 billion, involving a minority stake from Corpay. Upon closure in the first half of 2027, BILL will delist from public exchanges, with TPG acquiring a majority interest to integrate BILL’s financial operations with existing payment capabilities.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Claude Fable 5.2 hands-on: nearly tied on three custom accounting, coding, and data tasks, but Fable used far more tokens and cost 5x+ as much (Jessica Wachtel/The New Stack)
item.description: Hands-on testing shows that OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 deliver near-identical performance across accounting, coding, and data tasks. However, Claude Fable 5.2 exhibits significantly higher token consumption, resulting in inference costs more than five times higher than its competitor.

item.title: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)
item.description: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as acting national cyber director to address escalating cyber threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities while awaiting Senate confirmation of Kirsten A. Davies. This move centralizes oversight to ensure policy cohesion during the transitional period.

item.title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei defended their $900 billion AI infrastructure commitments ahead of their IPO, emphasizing a balanced approach between rapid growth and responsible AI development. The founders reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining an atypical organizational culture while scaling computing resources.
